(a) the BACM is a reliable measure of cerebral blood flow, (b) the BACMs ability to measure changes in cerebral blood flow is reliable across different raters, and (c) the BACMS ability to measure changes within the same raters is also reliable.
the Brain Acoustic Monitoring System (BAMS) is a reliable tool for measuring cerebral blood flow (CBF) in the human brain and that it can detect differences between normal and abnormal brain states.

the development of the Brain Acoustic monitor and the evaluation of its use in clinical practice.
the development of a novel, non-invasive, non-ionizing, and low-cost method for the measurement of cerebral blood flow.
the study of the relationship between the cerebral blood flow and the acoustic properties of the human brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BAMS is a reliable tool for the measurement of cerebral blood flow.
the Brain Acoustic Monitoring system is a reliable and accurate tool to measure cerebral blood flow and cerebral autoregulation in healthy individuals.
the Brain Acoustic monitor is an accurate, reliable, and valid instrument that can be used in the clinical setting for the assessment of cerebral blood flow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BAMS is reliable and valid.
the Brain Acoustic Monitoring System (BAMS) is an innovative, non-invasive, and cost effective tool for measuring cerebral blood flow (CBF).

the brain is not as isolated from the rest of the body as previously thought.
the brain is a highly dynamic system, and that the brain is not just a passive recipient of sensory stimuli.
